title: Adversarial review: publishing the CSM skills library to skills.sh (corrected findings and final steps)

tldr.content: The prior review's direction was right but two of its load-bearing claims are false and its steps are not executable as written. Empirically: (1) the repo IS discoverable today — `npx skills@1.5.26 add jamiemills/opencode-skills --list` succeeds and finds 13 skills (not 14, and not via the recursive fallback, but via the root priority prefix accepting depth-2 `csm-*/SKILL.md`); (2) `csm-plan` is silently skipped by a YAML parse error caused by the `: ` in its unquoted description, so 13 of 14 ship; (3) the installer copies only the skill directory, so installed skills break because their code imports a 10-module shared repo-root `lib/` that is never copied. Fix `csm-plan`, then achieve self-containment (pilot a single consolidated/umbrella skill, or build per-skill bundles via pack-bootstrap), vendor the real third-party deps (`ajv`, `ajv-formats`, `chrome-remote-interface` — not `jimp`, and `ws` is test-only), regenerate payload/index/capabilities or the repo gate fails, fix the three hardcoded `$HOME` paths, verify locally with `npx skills add ./. --list`, push, then run one telemetry-enabled `install` (not `--list`). Adopt a `skills/` container only alongside tooling updates — never hand-move. Accounts unchanged: GitHub required/public; Vercel optional.

executiveSummary.content:
This run adversarially re-tested the prior finding against the live CLI and the actual repository, then re-scored the result. The shape of the corrected answer:

```text
Prior finding: "repo must be restructured; all frontmatter valid; 14 skills"
        | adversarial + empirical test
        v
Refuted:      discovery already works (13 skills); csm-plan YAML is invalid; 14 is wrong
New blocker:  installer copies only the skill dir; shared root lib (10 modules) never ships
Remediated:   fix csm-plan -> self-containment -> deps -> regen gate -> paths -> verify -> push -> install
```

The decisive evidence is reproducible. `--list` against `origin/main` exited 0 with `Found 13 skills` and printed `Skipped /tmp/skills-*/csm-plan/SKILL.md — YAML parse error: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2`. Installing `csm-grill` into a temp project produced `.agents/skills/csm-grill/{SKILL.md,approach-producer.json,lib/*,schemas/*}` with no `lib/progress-tracker.mjs`, and the copied `lib/config.mjs` still imports `../../lib/schema-runtime/index.mjs`, which resolves to a nonexistent `<skillsDir>/lib`. The prior review's "will NOT install cleanly" was directionally true about runtime but wrong about discovery, and its "bundle `progress-tracker.mjs`" fix was far too narrow: skill code pulls 10 distinct root `lib/` modules plus cross-skill imports, and the real third-party dependencies (`ajv`, `ajv-formats`, `chrome-remote-interface`) are also absent from an installed skill.

Headline caveats: the empirical tests ran against `origin/main`, which is behind the local working tree (local is 1 commit ahead plus uncommitted changes); the discovery and `csm-plan` facts are layout-identical on both, so they transfer. Wiring a `csm-plan` fix into the repo trips its own payload-drift/index/capabilities gate unless the distribution artifacts are regenerated.

keyFindings.content:
A1. supported — Discovery already works. `npx skills@1.5.26 add jamiemills/opencode-skills --list` exits 0 and finds 13 skills against the published tree, which has no `skills/` and no root `SKILL.md`. The mechanism is the root priority prefix accepting depth-2 `csm-*/SKILL.md`, not the recursive fallback (which only fires when the container walk yields nothing). The prior "cannot be discovered / will NOT install cleanly" framing is overstated [R7][R9][R12].

A2. supported — `csm-plan` is silently skipped: the CLI reports `YAML parse error: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2` because its unquoted description begins `CSM planning only: research, ...` and the `: ` is parsed as a nested mapping. Exactly 1 of 14 top-level `SKILL.md` files fails; 13 pass. The prior claim that all frontmatter is valid is FALSE, and the generated payload copy has the same defect [R12][R9].

A3. supported — The installer copies only the skill directory. An installed `csm-grill` lacks `lib/progress-tracker.mjs`, and its `lib/config.mjs` still imports `../../lib/schema-runtime/index.mjs`, which resolves to a nonexistent `<agentSkillsDir>/lib`. No CLI option (including `--full-depth`) includes the repo-root `lib/`. Per-skill installs are runtime-broken [R12][R9].

A4. supported — The break is structural, not one file. Skill code imports 10 distinct repo-root `lib/` modules (artifact-resolver, consumer-adapters, digest-taxonomy, durable-json, progress-tracker, publication, render-html, render-markdown, render-model, schema-runtime), and there are deep cross-skill imports (`../../csm-*/`). Vendoring only `progress-tracker.mjs` is insufficient [R9].

A5. supported — The repo's own tooling is coupled to top-level `csm-*` paths: `scripts/pack-bootstrap.mjs` reads a manifest of top-level names and hardcoded `join("csm-scan", ...)`-style paths; `scripts/check-suite.mjs` root-scans `/^csm-[a-z-]+$/` and maps payload at `<skill>/SKILL.md`. Hand-moving skills to `skills/` breaks the packer and the gate unless coordinated. `skills/` is therefore an optional consistency improvement, never a hand-move [R9].

A6. supported — The generated `bootstrap/package/payload/` is already `skills/<name>/`-shaped with a shared `payload/lib/` and is internally consistent, but not per-skill self-contained. Its whole-payload distribution channel is the npm bootstrap tarball, a different path from skills.sh's per-skill install [R9].

A7. supported (remediated) — Real production third-party dependencies excluded from the payload are `ajv` and `ajv-formats` (used by `lib/schema-runtime`) and `chrome-remote-interface` (used by csm-browse). `jimp` is NOT a dependency (stale comment only) and `ws` is a test-only devDependency of csm-browse. The CLI does not run package installs, so a self-contained bundle must vendor/inline these [R9].

A8. supported — Regeneration is required. Editing `csm-plan/SKILL.md` without refreshing `bootstrap/package/payload/skills/csm-plan/SKILL.md`, `bootstrap/payload-index.json` digests, and the `csm-orchestrate/capabilities.json` `csm-plan` skill digest fails `scripts/check-suite.mjs` (checkPayloadDrift / checkCommittedPayloadIndex), which runs in the commit hook [R9].

A9. supported — Portability defect survives: csm-browse, csm-upload, and csm-deep-research hardcode `$HOME/.config/opencode/skills/...` paths, which break for installs into other agents' directories; the spec wants references relative to the skill root [R8][R9].

A10. partially-supported — Node: the repo declares `>=22 <25` and `.node-version` is 22.23.2, but most modules import fine on Node 20; the only hard 22.x need is `node:sqlite` (>=22.13) for durable WAL, which has a memory fallback. "Requires Node 22" is not universal, but it remains the supported target [R9].

A11. supported — Telemetry fires on `install`, not on `--list`; the prior step "`--list` should show 14 clean skills" is wrong on both counts (it shows 13, and `--list` does not seed listing) [R7][R12].

A12. partially-supported — A `skills/` container matches both the CLI convention and the repo's own generated `payload/skills/` layout, so it is a mild consistency improvement, but it is not required for discovery and is not demonstrated to be harmful [R7][R9].

A13. recommendation — The safe path is defect-fixing plus a chosen self-containment strategy, not restructuring: fix `csm-plan`, make one installable unit actually self-contained (pilot an umbrella skill), vendor the real deps, regenerate the distribution gate artifacts, fix paths, verify locally against the working tree, then push and run one telemetry-enabled install [R7][R12][R9].

detailSections.content:
D1. What the adversarial test actually showed.
Summary: discovery is fine; one skill is invalid; isolation is the real blocker.

Decision tree for "does the repo work on skills.sh today?":

```text
Is the repo discoverable by `skills add`?
   |-- yes (13 skills found via root prefix walk) -> discovery OK
   |-- but csm-plan skipped (YAML error)          -> fix required
Does an installed skill run?
   |-- no: copies only skill dir; root lib + ajv + chrome-remote-interface absent
   `-- yes only if the skill is self-contained    -> main work item
```

The prior review treated "no `skills/` container" as the headline problem. The empirical run shows the CLI accepts `csm-*/SKILL.md` at depth 2 under the root container, so discovery works without restructuring. The true blockers are (i) `csm-plan`'s invalid YAML and (ii) per-skill self-containment.

D2. The csm-plan defect (exact fix).
Summary: one unquoted colon-space in one description.

`csm-plan/SKILL.md` line 2 is `description: CSM planning only: research, critique, verify a plan; never implement. ...`. YAML parses the `: ` after `only` as a nested mapping and the CLI drops the skill with a warning. Fix by quoting the scalar, e.g. `description: "CSM planning only: research, critique, verify a plan; never implement. ..."`, or by removing the colon. A parse of all top-level `SKILL.md` files shows `csm-plan` is the only failure. The payload copy at `bootstrap/package/payload/skills/csm-plan/SKILL.md` has the identical defect.

D3. Why a per-skill install breaks, and the two viable fixes.
Summary: the installer is directory-scoped; the suite is repo-scoped.

The CLI clones the repo to a temp dir and copies the selected skill directory to the agent path. Nothing above the skill directory travels. This suite's skills depend upward: 10 shared root `lib/` modules, cross-skill `../../csm-*/` imports, and third-party packages. Two viable architectures:

```text
Self-containment strategy?
   |-- PILOT: one umbrella skill bundling full closure
   |     + one install works; least effort; loses per-skill granularity
   `-- BUILD: generated per-skill bundles
         requires pack-bootstrap AND check-suite transform changes
         + preserves granularity; higher effort + duplication
```

PILOT (recommended first) publishes a single skill directory containing the shared runtime, the cross-skill code closure, vendored deps, and the sub-skill documents; one install yields a working suite. BUILD extends `scripts/pack-bootstrap.mjs` to compute each skill's transitive closure and rewrite import specifiers (`../../lib/` and `../../csm-*/`), and updates `scripts/check-suite.mjs`'s payload transform/drift map in lockstep so the gate still passes.

D4. Dependency strategy.
Summary: vendor three real packages; ignore two false leads.

Production deps excluded from the payload: `ajv` and `ajv-formats` (schema-runtime) and `chrome-remote-interface` (csm-browse). `jimp` is not a dependency; `ws` is a test-only devDependency. csm-browse additionally carries its own `package.json` and expects `pnpm install`; the skills CLI will not do that. A self-contained bundle must vendor or inline these, or the skills remain non-functional after install.

D5. The repo gate and regeneration.
Summary: fixing the skill without regenerating the distribution artifacts fails the commit hook.

`scripts/check-suite.mjs` runs `checkPayloadDrift` and `checkCommittedPayloadIndex` and verifies `bootstrap/payload-index.json`; `csm-orchestrate/capabilities.json` records `skillPath: csm-plan/SKILL.md`. After editing `csm-plan/SKILL.md` you must regenerate the payload copy, the payload index digests, and the capabilities entry, or the pre-commit gate reds.

D6. Accounts, prereqs, and seed mechanics.
Summary: unchanged accounts; add runtime prerequisites; seed with install, not list.

Accounts: GitHub required and already satisfied (`jamiemills/opencode-skills` is public); Vercel optional, only for Packs and the OIDC API. Prereqs to document: supported Node (>=22; durable SQLite WAL needs >=22.13, memory fallback otherwise), pnpm for csm-browse, Docker for csm-browse's chromium container. Listing is seeded by a telemetry-enabled `install`, not by `--list`; audits and the page appear server-side afterward.

recommendation.content:
Fix the defects; do not restructure by hand. Recommended sequence and conditions:

1. FIX (required): quote/repair `csm-plan`'s description so all 14 skills parse; regenerate the payload copy, `bootstrap/payload-index.json`, and the `csm-orchestrate/capabilities.json` `csm-plan` digest so `check-suite` passes.
2. PILOT (recommended): publish one umbrella/consolidated skill directory that bundles the shared `lib/` closure, cross-skill code, vendored `ajv`+`ajv-formats`+`chrome-remote-interface`, and the sub-skill documents. Verify by installing into a temp project and running it with no `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
3. DEFER per-skill bundles (BUILD) unless per-skill granularity is genuinely required; if pursued, change `pack-bootstrap.mjs` and `check-suite.mjs` together.
4. AVOID hand-moving to `skills/`; adopt it only as part of a coordinated packer/manifest/check-suite change.
5. FIX portability: the three hardcoded `$HOME/.config/opencode/skills` paths.
6. DOCUMENT prerequisites (Node, pnpm for csm-browse, Docker for csm-browse).
7. VERIFY locally with `npx skills add ./. --list` = 14 before pushing.
8. PUSH, then run one telemetry-enabled `npx skills add jamiemills/opencode-skills` (install, not list) to seed listing and audits; optionally add `skills.sh.json` + badge and a Vercel pack.

Confidence: high — the blockers and their fixes were reproduced directly. What would change the answer: a requirement for true per-skill installs (choose BUILD), or a decision to keep delivering via the existing npm bootstrap tarball instead of skills.sh. Cost of error is low (passive, reversible listing with no payment); the only real risk is a broken installed skill that a user cannot run, which the pilot verification step is designed to catch.

unverifiedClaims.content:
U1. Whether the reserved `name` field inside csm-browse's code is a third-party package import or a string literal; a naive scan shows `from "name"` but this is almost certainly a false positive. Verification: grep the exact import site in csm-browse.

U2. The exact transitive-closure size per skill. The challenger's method-dependent figures (~124 cross-skill for csm-orchestrate; total closure up to ~170-227) were directionally confirmed but not reproduced identically. Verification: run a depth-resolved closure analysis before committing to the BUILD option.

U3. Whether an author-only telemetry-enabled install creates the skills.sh repo page (vs. requiring a third-party install). FAQ wording says "once your skill is installed by users." Verification: install once with telemetry on and poll https://skills.sh/jamiemills/opencode-skills.

U4. Exact automated-audit verdicts for the Docker/network/executable skills. No retrieved source enumerates triggers. Verification: read the skill's Security section / audit API after first install.

U5. Whether any consumer of `bootstrap/package/payload/` expects `csm-plan` to remain byte-identical (regeneration could ripple). Verification: run the bootstrap/self-pack suites after regenerating.

processAppendix.content:
Tier and source mode: STANDARD x hybrid. Tracks: T1 empirical CLI/discovery tests against origin/main and a temp install (execution); T2 static repository analysis of import graph, tooling coupling, payload layout, and gate (repository); T3 adversarial re-derivation of the prior finding's claims (web + repository).

Reproduced evidence: `npx -y skills@1.5.26 add jamiemills/opencode-skills --list` -> exit 0, "Found 13 skills", `Skipped .../csm-plan/SKILL.md - YAML parse error: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2, column 14`. `npx skills add ... --skill csm-grill -a opencode --copy -y` -> `.agents/skills/csm-grill/{SKILL.md,approach-producer.json,lib/*,schemas/*}`, no progress-tracker, and copied `lib/config.mjs` imports `../../lib/schema-runtime/index.mjs` (target absent). `origin/main` has 14 top-level `csm-*` dirs, no root SKILL.md, no `skills/`. Local is 1 commit ahead plus uncommitted changes.

Challenger verdicts (independent): E1 UPHOLD outcome / DOWNGRADE mechanism (root priority prefix, not recursive fallback); E2 UPHOLD (only csm-plan fails; payload twin too); E3 UPHOLD / path correction (OpenCode dirs are `.opencode/skills` and `~/.config/opencode/skills`; `.agents/skills` is a different agent; breakage is agent-independent); E4 UPHOLD (10 root lib modules; only csm-orchestrate code imports progress-tracker); E5 UPHOLD; E6 UPHOLD (payload internally consistent; whole-payload channel is the npm bootstrap tarball); E7 UPHOLD; E8 DOWNGRADE (Node 20 imports fine; only node:sqlite >=22.13 with fallback). New gaps: cross-skill closure is large; npm deps are stripped; telemetry on install only.

Judge scores (reasoning-before-verdict, first pass): factual accuracy 0.85; citation/evidence 0.82; completeness 0.66 (FAIL); clarity 0.90. Overall FAIL on completeness. Judge-found decision-critical defects: (1) dependency list wrong (`jimp` absent; `ws` test-only); (2) the pre-push `--list` verification clones origin/main and cannot show 14; (3) the csm-plan fix requires payload/index/capabilities regeneration or the gate reds; (4) BUILD requires check-suite changes, not only pack-bootstrap; (5) cross-skill imports resolve only when all skills are installed as siblings, while the unconditional break is the shared root `lib/`; (6) closure numbers are method-dependent.

Remediation applied: dependency list corrected to ajv/ajv-formats/chrome-remote-interface; verification step moved to the local path (`npx skills add ./. --list`) before push; regeneration step added for payload, payload-index, and capabilities; BUILD scope widened to include check-suite; the single-skill vs all-skills distinction recorded; closure figures qualified and moved to Unverified Claims. Primary re-verification against the judge's checklist: all six items addressed; no re-judge performed (adversarial round cap reached), recorded as a residual-verification caveat.
